findings.title: Cron job fetches and executes remote code as root
findings.why_suspicious: Runs every minute as root and pipes a remote download straight into a shell. Matches the high-severity cron pattern in references/linux_indicators.md.
findings.recommended_action: Review the file. If unrecognized, isolate the host and quarantine the file using a dedicated remediation tool. PhageGuard will not modify it.

findings.title: SUID bit set on an interpreter in a non-standard path
findings.why_suspicious: A root-owned SUID interpreter under /tmp is a classic privilege-escalation backdoor. Not in the SUID allowlist.
findings.recommended_action: Do not execute it. Capture its hash, then review with a remediation workflow.

findings.title: Unexpected listener bound to all interfaces on a high port
findings.why_suspicious: A shell owning a socket listening on all interfaces is reverse-shell shaped. Correlated with process inventory.
findings.recommended_action: Identify pid 20413 and the parent process. If unrecognized, treat as active compromise.

findings.title: Config files in /etc changed during a package update window
findings.why_suspicious: Recent change, but timestamp aligns with an unattended-upgrades run. Likely benign; surfaced for completeness.
findings.recommended_action: No action needed unless the change is unexplained.

summary: 2 high, 1 medium, 1 info. Two findings (F-001, F-002) are strongly consistent with an active compromise and warrant immediate review. ClamAV and YARA were not installed, so signature/rule scans were skipped.
next_steps: Review F-001 and F-002 immediately; consider isolating the host
Identify the process behind the listener in F-003
Install ClamAV and YARA to enable signature and rule-based scans (Phase 2)
